title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a (real 2-dimensional) surface and x a point of X. On the previous page Grothendieck built the 'local fundamental groupoid' Chemins(X,x). Its objects are germs of arcs γ issuing from x. A morphism γ→γ' is an isomorphism, over the punctured disc D_x^*, between the universal coverings of D_x^* pointed by γ and by γ'. This gives an equivalence Chemins(X,x) ≃ Revêtements(D_x^*) ≃ Π_1(D_x^*).

On this page X is assumed differentiable at x. (76) defines Cheminsdiff(X,x) as the full subcategory of differentiable arc-germs. These are germs whose tangent map at the origin is injective, so each has a well-defined half-tangent u ∈ S_x. (77) S_x is the space of half-lines (rays) of T_x X, which is ≅ S^1. (78) recalls Π_1(S_x) ≃ Revuniv(S_x). (79) announces an equivalence Cheminsdiff(X,x) → Π_1(S_x) which, on objects, sends a differentiable arc to its half-tangent. It is compatible with the identifications with universal coverings of D_x^* and of S_x.

So one must give a canonical bijection Isom(γ,γ') ≅ {homotopy classes of paths in S_x from u to u'}. The next page does this indirectly. It builds a functor Θ: Π_1(S_x) → Revêtements(D_x^*) using the poset A_x of closed proper arcs of the circle S_x. It uses the fact that the groupoid of fractions of this poset is canonically equivalent to Π_1(S_x). The geometric content: to an arc of directions one attaches the sector of D_x^* it spans. A sector is contractible, so it gives a canonical sheet (base-point) of the universal covering of D_x^*.

In modern terms: differentiable arc-germs are 'tangential base points'. The punctured neighbourhood D_x^* is homotopy equivalent, via the oriented real blow-up of x, to its boundary circle S_x. A differentiable arc lifts to the blow-up, ending at its half-tangent. Paths in the circle of directions therefore compute local monodromy between tangential base points. This serves the Longue Marche programme: fundamental groupoids of (real models of) curves based at points 'at the punctures', in the spirit of Galois–Teichmüller theory.
errors: No mathematical error. Implicit hypotheses: X is a 2-dimensional manifold near x, so that S_x ≅ S^1; and 'differentiable arc' means a germ with nonzero derivative at 0 (as on the previous page).

The functor (79) is an equivalence but not injective on objects: distinct arcs with the same half-tangent become canonically isomorphic. This is consistent and is in fact the point of the construction.

ideas.what: Germs of differentiable arcs at x, up to the local fundamental groupoid, are classified by their half-tangent. The full subcategory of differentiable arcs is equivalent to Π_1 of the circle of directions S_x.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points; oriented real blow-up (circle of directions) as model for the punctured neighbourhood
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points, 1989) for tangential base points; A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama for real oriented blow-ups
ideas.where_published: Ideas on base points at punctures appear in La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this precise differentiable/half-tangent formulation unsure

ideas.what: Local fundamental groupoid at x defined with arc-germs as objects and isomorphisms of pointed universal coverings of D_x^* as morphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Local fundamental groupoid / fundamental groupoid with a set of (tangential) base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 style fibre-functor groupoids), Brown (groupoids with many base points)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (groupoid of fibre functors), La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Π_1(S^1) computed as the enveloping groupoid (groupoid of fractions) of the poset of closed proper arcs (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid of fractions of a poset of contractible subsets models Π_1 (Quillen/McCord-type covering theorem)

missed.claim: An explicit topological/differential construction of tangential base points: differentiable arc-germs mapped to half-tangents, giving an equivalence of local groupoids with Π_1(circle of directions). This is done in an unpublished text that likely predates or parallels Deligne's 1989 tangential base points, with an elementary sector/poset construction.
missed.quote: Je vais définir une équivalence de catégories (79) Cheminsdiff(X,x) ≈→ Π_1(S_x) qui, sur les ensembles d'objets, soit l'application associant à tout germe d'arc différentiable en x sa demi-tangente
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own version of tangential base points in the Longue Marche continuation, relevant to crediting the idea. The construction is standard today (real blow-up), so the novelty is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, essentially complete formulation of tangential base points via half-tangents and the circle of directions in unpublished notes. Historically interesting priority-wise, but mathematically standard and close to known Longue Marche themes.
transcription_corrections: (76) and later: 'Germesrevdiff(X,x)' / 'Germesrev(X,x)' should read 'Cheminsdiff(X,x)' / 'Chemins(X,x)', consistent with the previous page.
Line 1: 'Soit d'autre part, dans le cas où X est diff. en x,' is correct.
In the diagram under (79), the vertical arrows read ≀ (equivalences) to Revuniv(D_x^*) and Revuniv(S_x); the right one is written as 'Revuniv(S_x)'.
